items.checkbox: Replace the prototype's nearest-index links with a time-sync that adds no links or components. Define sorted/duplicate/NaT, tie and maximum-offset behavior.') and D-contract 656-659 ('WP4 uses identity ComponentLinks on precomputed nearest-index components'). Build it inside the per-viewer solar:frame_time tool (glue_solar/tools.py FrameTimeTool), which glue_solar.setup() already adds to every ImageViewer, so late-opened and session-restored viewers join automatically. The tool gets an explicit master (a checkable 'Drive time' action, default the SJI viewer); followers' state.slices change on frame/step axes only; nearest indices come from the #52 `Time` components (argsort, so descending V34 step times work, cached per dataset pair); and each follower's label shows the signed offset. Proposed defaults for the user to confirm: pair by OBSID+STARTOBS; a tie goes to the earlier frame; when |Δ| exceeds half the follower's median cadence, move to the nearest frame but label it 'NO MATCH Δ=…'; a raster map, whose step axis is displayed, represents its scan by an adjustable 'raster timing step' (default: the selected point's step, else mid-raster), which is the CRISPEX timing offset.

items.checkbox: New item; the plan has no Doppler image, and the plan:857-859 two-wavelength blink does not subtract. Add a D4 `layer_action` 'Doppler image…' (glue_qt/config.py:220@0.4.2) for a raster window whose rest wavelength comes from the WP5 policy. It adds one derived dataset D(Δv) = I(λ0(1+Δv/c)) − I(λ0(1−Δv/c)), red minus blue, computed with np.interp on the Å axis and NaN wherever a wing is masked or outside the window. D is either a cube over Δv browsed with the ordinary slider (CRISPEX's mirrored lp_dop image) or a single ±v map (the tutorials' ±50 km/s Mg II Dopplergram). Link its spatial pixel axes to the source as WP2 does, and open no viewer. Record the sign convention in the component name and meta, since IRIS-9 and ITN26 disagree, and reuse the WP5 per-dataset wavelength offset for drift.
items.done_when: A synthetic Gaussian shifted by +10 km/s gives D>0 at Δv=10 km/s and D=0 at Δv=0. On ~/DATA/IRIS 20180102 3610108077 Mg II k with rest 2796.35 Å, the ±50 km/s map equals a numpy np.interp reference to float32 precision, and fill/masked samples come out NaN. A Pixel click on the Doppler map drives the source raster's point. A window with no rest wavelength is rejected with a message and no partial dataset.
depends_on: WP10 M0 -200 fill published as NaN

items.checkbox: Refines plan:727-742, e.g. 'Blank rest uses irispy's default; blank wings use the whole window; one wing alone is an error.' Take the rest from the WP5 policy. Require wings, defaulting to ±0.5 Å or prefilled from the Profile range tool's `x_range`; this pulls the plan:1023 deferral into v1. Add an optional continuum window whose mean is subtracted before `irispy.utils.moments.calculate_moments` and published as `I(cont)`. Name the widths `sigma`/`velocity_sigma` and document FWHM = 2.355σ. NaN Inf/saturated samples before irispy zeroes them. Build coords as `_GlueWCS(SlicedLowLevelWCS(...))` so WP3 can save the maps. Run above about 5e7 elements in the existing `glue_qt.utils.threading.Worker`. Label Mg II and C II products as proxies. Ierr/Verr error maps wait for uncertainty propagation in irispy.
items.done_when: A synthetic SpectrogramCube with a known Gaussian plus noise, missing samples and Inf recovers centroid, sigma and velocity. On ~/DATA/IRIS 20180102 3610108077 with ±0.5 Å around 2796.35 Å, the median Mg II k velocity satisfies |v| < 5 km/s; the review measured −0.5 km/s here, against +504.5 km/s with the whole-window defaults. I(cont) and the continuum-subtracted intensity equal a numpy reference. The maps round-trip through a WP3 session. GUI-thread blocking is at most 0.5 s on 20130902 4000255147 Si IV. The user-guide page shows choosing Int/Vel/sigma/I(cont) in the Image attribute combo.
depends_on: WP10 M0 -200 fill / negative-step mask fixes

items.checkbox: Refines plan:875-880 and plan:894-902 ('Keep masks/weights, fit-window controls, velocity/net-flux derived maps and diagnostics files out of v1'). In v1: use the WP2 rest/wings fields as the fit window and emit `velocity` (optical convention, WP5 rest) and |sigma|. Pass `mask = loader mask | ~isfinite` to `parallel_fit_dask(mask=...)` in place of clipping and nan_to_num. NaN fits with sigma ≤ 0, amplitude ≤ 0 or a centroid outside the window, and report the rejected fraction. Make the residual opt-in and float32. Default to a single Gaussian, and label Mg II/C II double fits as proxies.
items.done_when: Noisy synthetic cubes with missing and Inf samples recover amplitude, centroid and sigma. On ~/DATA/IRIS 20180102 3610108077 Si IV 1403, no fully masked spectrum gets a finite fit (today 1687/1687 do), and the rejected fraction is shown. Velocity equals the WP5 conversion of the centroid. The recorded tests include a 4D stack case. A Mg II k single-Gaussian fit keeps its median centroid near the review's 2796.345 Å.

items.checkbox: Refines plan:495 ('Fit already fits a selected 1D profile using Gaussian/polynomial models'). In `setup()`, register 'Gaussian + constant' and 'two Gaussians + constant' single-spectrum fitters through glue's public `fit_plugin` registry (glue/config.py:815@1.27.0), each an `AstropyFitter1D` over an astropy `custom_model` shared with WP6. The Profile Fit tab then fits the point- or ROI-mean spectrum that the Pixel tool or an ROI subset already produces, matching iris_sum_spec + spec_gauss_iris. Rescale x internally so that fits converge on metre and Å axes alike. The Fit tab calls `build_and_fit(x, y)` with no dy, so document the fit as unweighted.
items.done_when: Probe run (work-5/test_w5_probe.py, released 0.4.2): the registered fitter appears in the Fit tab as ['Polynomial', 'Gaussian', 'Gaussian + constant (probe)']. With x in metres it returned its seeds unchanged (mean 1.40272e-07 m, stddev 2.05e-10 m), so x rescaling is required; the cause is probably conditioning, which is unverified. The item is done when, on the irispy 20210905 and ~/DATA/IRIS 20180102 Si IV 1403 rasters, Fit-tab fits of a Pixel-point spectrum and an ROI-mean spectrum match a direct astropy fit to 1e-6 relative in both m and Å display. The guide must also carry the recipe: ROI mean spectrum, zoom to 2794-2799 Å, fit.

done.how: Image and Profile slice sliders have first/prev/back/stop/forward/next/last buttons driven by a QTimer (glue_qt/viewers/common/data_slice_widget.py:81-83,146-193 at glue-qt 0.4.2). The interval is round(500/|n|) ms, speeding up with repeated presses, and playback wraps. A focused slider steps with the arrow keys. Docs, including the Tab/Backspace conflicts, are in wp9-temporal-docs. CRISPEX-style frame shortcuts belong to the WP11 keyboard item (F197).

Load a raster (default view wavelength × slit, the spectrogram) and press play on its step/exposure slider (data_slice_widget.py playback). Documented in wp9-temporal-docs; movie export is the WP12 movie item (F178/F179).

The IRIS browser lists every SJI (keyed by TDESC1) and aligned AIA cutout of an observation, with no channel limit (glue_solar/sources/loaders/scan.py:164-165,174-175; loaders/iris.py:121-125,240-242 at 236f0a8). Each loads as a Data with an irissji/sdoaia colormap and can be opened from the data collection. Multi-SJI coordination is wp4-sji-panels and wp4-time-sync; docs are in wp9-temporal-docs.

Tick 'Stack sequential raster scans' in the browser (iris_loader.ui:107-112), or call raster_data(files, stack=True). Either gives a (scan, step, slit, wavelength) float memmap with a per-pixel datetime64 Time (loaders/iris.py:104-113,153-175; stack_spectrograms.py at 236f0a8). The scan-0 WCS limit is wp1-stack-per-scan-wcs, and per-scan exposure times are in wp4-exposure-readout.

The browser lists each observation's SJI channels as checkboxes (loaders/iris.py:240,262-267), and loaded channels open from the data collection. wp4-sji-panels makes the preset open every selected channel. Thumbnails are deliberately not built, per plan non-goal 1012 ('No full IDL widget/UI clone').

SJI files load as 3D Glue cubes with a gWCS time axis (loaders/iris.py:121-142). The time slider and playback replace a map-array movie. irispy SJICube.to_maps exists if a sunpy map sequence is ever needed.

Open 'IRIS: browse observations…'. Each observation is one row showing STARTOBS, OBSID, description (OBS_DESC, falling back to an ObsID decode), XCEN, YCEN and SAT_ROT (scan.py:54-68,101-107 and iris.py:228-239@236f0a8). No OBS_DEC fallback is needed: a header probe of all 130 FITS files in ~/DATA/IRIS (2013-2026, iris-plan env) found OBS_DESC in 129 and OBS_DEC in none; the one file without OBS_DESC is the derived rb_steps file. Docs item: wp9-browser-export-overlay-docs.

Tick rows or children in the browser and press 'Load selected' (iris.py:195,280-315@236f0a8), or use File→Open, which routes through the 'IRIS Level 2 FITS' data_factory (sources/iris.py:23-28). Non-FITS files are never listed (scan.py:145-150). An optional double-click shortcut is part of wp8-browser-conveniences. Docs item: wp9-browser-export-overlay-docs.

Tick an SJI in the browser and press 'Load selected'. The first SJI/AIA cube opens in an Image viewer (sources/iris.py:62-65) with transparent NaN padding (#53). Play it with the slice-widget playback buttons (released glue-qt 0.4.2 data_slice_widget.py:50-89,146) and adjust contrast with the stock stretches (glue/config.py:839-842@1.27.0). The missing gamma stretch belongs to the WP11 scaling item (F062), not here. Docs item: wp9-browser-export-overlay-docs.

IRIS masks load as a boolean '<label> mask' component (loaders/iris.py:79-80). An x-range selection in a Histogram viewer, or 'Create faceted subsets', gives a subset that is drawn as a filled overlay in every viewer of that dataset. A probe in the iris-plan env confirmed that a bool component has kind 'numerical' and that RangeSubsetState(0.5,1.5) selects exactly the masked pixels. An external integer FITS mask cube with the dataset's shape loads through the layer action 'Import subset mask(s)' (glue/io/formats/fits/subset_mask.py@1.27.0); masknt=1 cubes must be broadcast first. Contours are not built; a filled subset with alpha is the equivalent. Docs item: wp9-browser-export-overlay-docs.

Each viewer's layer style editor sets colour, alpha and linewidth per layer. Preferences sets foreground and background, the default data colour and alpha, and the font size (glue-qt app/preferences.py). Docs item: wp9-browser-export-overlay-docs.

In any viewer, use toolbar Save → 'Save plot to file' (mpl:save → matplotlib save_figure, glue_qt/viewers/matplotlib/toolbar.py:66-75@0.4.2). A probe in the iris-plan env found these Agg file types: avif, eps, gif, jpeg, jpg, pdf, pgf, png, ps, raw, rgba, svg, svgz, tif, tiff, webp. Docs item wp9-browser-export-overlay-docs documents this and rewords the plan:1012-1013 'PostScript workflow' non-goal to mean the IDL PS-device workflow.

Separate Image viewers of one raster keep independent wavelength sliders. For the lock, Profile Options → Navigate moves the wavelength slice of every open Image viewer showing that dataset together (glue_qt/viewers/profile/profile_tools.py:140-161 @ glue-qt 0.4.2, iris-plan env). Caveat: on 0.4.2, Navigate lands on the wrong slice when the display unit is not the native one ('slice 28, expected 20' in feas-markers-panels/released.log). WP1's native Å or Qt #70 fixes this. Documented by wp9-m0-existing-workflow-recipes.

Profile Options y_min/y_max (glue/viewers/matplotlib/state.py:127-128@1.27.0), per-layer linewidth (glue/viewers/profile/state.py:349) and the axes-editor label/tick sizes. The CRISPEX replay step 02 set ylim (-5, 50). Noted in wp9-m3-spectral-recipes.

Each window gets its own Profile viewer, which autoscales on its own (wp4-m1-multi-window). Profile Normalize rescales each layer to [0,1] (glue/viewers/profile/state.py:50-51,411-412@1.27.0). The normalised range is only meaningful once the WP10 -200 fill fix lands (replay step 02 gave normalized_range (-200, 7.25)). Noted in wp9-m3-spectral-recipes.

Axis-label text fields in the Profile axes editor (glue_qt/viewers/matplotlib/axes_editor.ui:82,175). The Profile rewrites the x label when x_att changes (glue/viewers/profile/viewer.py:15-31@1.27.0). Priority 'wont', so no further work. Noted in wp9-m3-spectral-recipes.

The stock Slice tool's ClickRoiMode path: a click adds a vertex, dragging updates it, Enter finishes and Esc aborts (glue/viewers/matplotlib/toolbar_mode.py:188-230@1.27.0; used by glue_qt pv_slicer and core BasePathSlicerMode). Remove-last-vertex, a spline and rubber-band preview are accepted gaps. Saved paths are covered in wp12-m3-path-extras. Documented by wp9-m0-existing-workflow-recipes.

The default raster view is the wavelength × slit spectrogram, and the step slider (with playback) moves through each raster position's panel. A per-position panel grid falls under the 'no full IDL widget clone' non-goal (plan 1012). The plan row at 388 should note that iris_xraster's 'Spectroheliogram' label means per-position spectrogram panels. Documented by wp9-m0-existing-workflow-recipes.

The browser shows STARTOBS and OBSID columns (loaders/iris_loader.ui:62-67@main), and every dataset label embeds OBSID-STARTOBS (loaders/iris.py _observation_label@main). DATE_OBS is available via Ctrl+I.

The Image viewer's layer style editor has v_min/v_max, percentile presets, stretch (log among them, glue/config.py:839-842@1.27.0), flip, contrast/bias and reset, plus the image:contrast_bias drag tool. Documented by wp9-display-window-basics.

Each ImageLayerState has its own v_min/v_max/percentile (glue/viewers/image/state.py:491-560@1.27.0), and each spectral window and SJI channel is its own dataset, so Si IV, Mg II and SJI keep separate scaling. Documented by wp9-display-window-basics.
Every viewer is a resizable QMdiSubWindow (glue-qt mdi_area.py). Documented by wp9-display-window-basics.
Canvas > Gather Windows (Ctrl+G) tiles the subwindows (glue_qt/app/application.py:861-863@0.4.2). 'Bring to front' does not apply to a single MDI main window. Documented by wp9-display-window-basics.
Covered by equivalents: separate glue processes run side by side, tabs can be renamed (Canvas > Rename Tab), and comparing windows maps to the WP5 blink checkbox. IDL window IDs have no counterpart.

Help > Version information lists every installed distribution, including glue-solar (application.py:817-822@0.4.2). Release notes come from the towncrier changelog, and auto-showing them is not needed.
`glue -v` for verbosity, `--faulthandler`, View > Console Log and Plugins > Plugin Manager (glue-qt main.py and application.py@0.4.2).

RETINA is covered by Qt's native HiDPI scaling, and the existing WP0 #68 font-clipping check (plan:333-337) stays as is. NO_SJI means leaving SJI channels unticked in the browser (loaders/iris.py:240-258@main). YOFFSETS is obsolete.

The Preferences dialog (colours, theme, font) loads plugin panes from the preference_panes registry (glue_qt/config.py:218@0.4.2). IRIS defaults come as per-dataset defaults from wp11-iris-display-defaults, not persisted settings, following the plan's no-persisted-settings rule for WP5/WP8.

File→Open uses the IRIS Level 2 data_factory (sources/iris.py:23-28, priority 200 over glue's FITS reader), or Plugins → 'IRIS: browse observations…' (sources/iris.py:47-65). raster_data/image_data load single scans, per-scan datasets, a 4D stack or a sit-and-stare cube through irispy (loaders/iris.py:133-175@236f0a8), and `glue file.glu` restores a session in place of data. Reads are eager (memmap=False); lazy access is tracked in wp10-m2-lazy-loading and docs in wp9-m0-inspection-scripting-docs.

The browser shows one checkbox per spectral window and passes the ticked ones to raster_data(files, windows=...), i.e. irispy spectral_windows (loaders/iris.py:153-175); each window stays its own dataset with its own grid and scaling. File→Open loads every window. Documented in wp9-m0-inspection-scripting-docs.

The CRISPEX SPECTFILE reference spectrum is available as the dataset's own layer in a Profile viewer with function set to Mean, beside the point/ROI subset profiles. The default function is Maximum (FUNCTIONS, glue/viewers/profile/state.py:22@1.27.0), so the user must select Mean; documented in wp9-m0-inspection-scripting-docs.

Data collection → 'Arithmetic attributes' (ArithmeticEditorWidget, glue_qt/app/application.py:423,487@0.4.2) defines a scaled derived component, e.g. `<window> * 2.5`. Documented in wp9-m0-inspection-scripting-docs.

The status-bar readout gives a per-dataset position in arcsec: solar:cursor_readout on released glue-qt 0.4.2 (glue_solar/tools.py:69-127, added when ImageViewer lacks cursor_status), or glue-qt's own readout after Qt #74. Values come through _GlueWCS (loaders/iris.py:35-69), and 'w' switches to pixels. The time-dependent SJI pointing is honoured: the map-4 probe read −52" at frame 0 and −10" at the last frame.
